solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relate to wounded bear …

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged and knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asked to empathise with an injured bear, the ellipsis hinting at more to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' sits at the end looking like the animal being related to, but it is the verb meaning to put up with; 'wounded' rearranges RELATE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure or put up with it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pocket in short pants

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, its last letter docked

parts.note: in American usage pants are the long-legged garment worn over underwear

explanation.surface: A pocket found inside a pair of shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short pants' reads as shorts, but 'short' only trims the garment's name. In Britain pants means underwear; here it is the American sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is informal for pocketing it, often dishonestly.

clue.text: Investigate family trapped in toilet, closed

indicators.note: trapped in means the relatives word is enclosed within the toilet word

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
a door that is pulled to is closed
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A family locked inside a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine or research a matter is a phrasal-verb synonym for investigating it.

clue.text: Man, superior one, and blunt

parts.note: arch means chief or principal, as in archenemy
I is the Roman numeral one
a bald statement is plain and blunt

explanation.surface: A description of a man: lofty, singular and outspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's given name, so any male name can be clued as a man.

clue.text: Old priest: perhaps Miguel's the one

parts.note: Miguel is a Spanish name, and el is the Spanish word for the
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asking whether Miguel is the ancient priest in question.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible he is the high priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel.

clue.text: not that tears help its suffering at first

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A claim that crying, rather than something else, eases its own suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first: 'not that' points to the nearer of the two demonstratives.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative for something near is contrasted with the one for something farther away, so it is the opposite choice.

clue.text: Boy goes out to get cuddly toys

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
a fire or light that goes out dies

explanation.surface: A boy heads out to fetch some soft toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy bears are the classic soft plush toys children cuddle.

clue.text: Sort of lettuce you see little of in the main

definitions.meaning: a crisp pale round-headed salad variety

definitions.text: you see little of in the main
definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, and most of a floating mass of frozen water lies below the surface

explanation.surface: A salad leaf that is rarely seen in main courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' looks like a main course, but it is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Only its tip shows above the water, so you see little of it at sea; it also names a crisp lettuce.

clue.text: Comb, note, regularly chosen for musical instrument

indicators.note: regularly chosen means every other letter is picked, here the second, fourth and so on of comb and note

explanation.surface: Someone noting that a comb can be played as a makeshift musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind of the orchestra is a classic example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Young rich lend extravagantly

indicators.note: doing something extravagantly is doing it wildly, so the letters of rich lend are thrown around

explanation.surface: Wealthy youngsters who lend money with abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' looks like an adjective for 'rich', but it is the noun sense, offspring collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's or person's young are its offspring, the kids of the family.

clue.text: Drinking game after end of parties

indicators.note: after places the synonym for game behind the letter from parties
end of picks the final letter of the word parties

parts.note: being game means being ready and willing to try something

explanation.surface: Someone drinking and playing a game once the parties are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a pastime, but it is the adjective meaning up for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulping liquor greedily is a synonym for drinking heavily.

clue.text: Sponsor rebuilt great pond

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together again in a new form, so the letters of great pond are rearranged

explanation.surface: A backer pays for a big pond to be reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponsor' looks like a funder, but here it is the religious sense: one who sponsors a child at baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening, the adult who vouches for the child is called its sponsor.

clue.text: Stray, right after hesitation

indicators.note: after puts the letter for right behind the hesitation sound

parts.note: er is the sound people make when they hesitate

explanation.surface: Someone wanders off course, turning right after a moment's hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray from what is correct is to go wrong or make a mistake, a synonym.

clue.text: A pint courtesy of Paddy?

parts.note: Paddy looks like an Irishman standing a round, but a paddy is a flooded field where rice grows, so the drink is brewed from its grain

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Paddy buys someone a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy is a common nickname for an Irishman; with a lower case p a paddy is a rice field.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink brewed from rice grain comes, punningly, from a paddy field.

clue.text: One in the eye ultimately for rude girl

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of each of the words for and rude

parts.note: Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A rude girl gets her comeuppance, a 'one in the eye' meaning a snub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in the eye' reads as the idiom for a rebuff, but literally it is a part found inside the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive membrane lining the back of the eyeball is one part found in the eye.

clue.text: Having arranged fee, find an address in Turkey

indicators.note: having arranged signals the letters of fee and find being put into a new order

explanation.surface: After agreeing a fee, someone tracks down a postal address in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a street location but is a form of address, a title.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a Turkish title of respect, used like sir for an educated man.

clue.text: Not when the golf club was fashionable, though

definitions.text: Not when the golf club was fashionable, though

parts.words: Not when the golf club was fashionable, though
parts.note: a golf club called an iron suggests an era when irons were in vogue, but the prehistoric period named after the metal had no golf at all

explanation.surface: Someone recalling the era when a certain golf club was all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the prehistoric period when tools were first made from the smelted metal, long before golf existed.

clue.text: Purpose of French Bull, Lion or Crab, for example

parts.note: de is the French word for of

parts.words: Bull, Lion or Crab, for example
parts.note: Taurus, Leo and Cancer are signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what French bulls, lions or crabs are for.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals on Bull, Lion and Crab hint at Taurus, Leo and Cancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by intention is doing it by plan or aim, so purpose is a synonym.

clue.text: Added comments to approving gesture when touring gallery

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the gesture word goes around the gallery name

parts.note: a nod of the head shows approval
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A visitor touring a gallery makes remarks and nods in approval.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain, chiefly in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing remarks or annotations on a text means adding comments to it.

clue.text: Two couples, speaking in favour

indicators.note: speaking says the word is to be taken as it sounds when said, not as spelt

parts.note: two pairs make a total of four

explanation.surface: Two couples speaking up in support of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pro a motion means supporting it, voting in favour.

clue.text: Not feeling pressure in very close finish

parts.note: a limb that has gone dead has no feeling
turning up the heat means applying pressure

explanation.surface: An athlete so numb they cannot sense the strain in a tight finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A race where two competitors cross the line together is a tie, the closest possible result.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, nude lad's to get off horse

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the letters of nude lad's come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A naked young man surprisingly has to dismount.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the seat from a mount, or throwing a rider, is to dismount someone from it.

clue.text: Welshman's daughter: excellent

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
A1 means first-class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: Praise for a Welshman's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British label for top quality, and the figure 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a typical Welsh male given name, the Welsh form of David.

clue.text: Following cross going into the goal

indicators.note: going into puts the cross mark inside the word for the goal

parts.note: in football the ball goes into the net
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A football cross that ends up in the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a football pass but is the X mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The one after, coming subsequently in order, is the following one.

clue.text: Long sentence in biography?

definitions.meaning: the longest prison term, imprisonment until death
a biography tells the story of someone's existence; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a biography is just one very long sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole-term prison sentence and a written account of a person's existence both go by this word.

clue.text: Some skint here, daily owing money

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people here are broke every day and in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skint' is British slang for having no money, which fits the surface's theme of debt.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn bank balance was traditionally printed in crimson ink, so the idiom means in debt.
